cohort: Malaysian citizens with singleton births, excluding incomplete data and ambiguous genitalia, from a single tertiary hospital between 2010-2013 and 2020-2023.
finding: There was no difference in the prevalence of adverse neonatal outcomes between the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods, although maternal age >35 years, premature birth, and Caesarean delivery were consistently identified as significant risk factors in both periods, with multiparity and male neonates also significant during the pandemic.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was a significant risk factor for adverse neonatal outcomes in both the pre-pandemic (aOR: 2.469) and pandemic (aOR: 2.32) periods.
